newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper settles flat, market well underpinned.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper settles flat, market well underpinned.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended unchanged Tuesday, slipping back from earlier fresh five-month highs, as the market remained well underpinned, dealers said.
Some buying near the close helped most active July avoid losses but all the other contracts ended weaker apart from August, September and October which posted slim gains.

"Funds came in and there is support not too far below the market," a dealer said. "Others went long with them and when there was no follow through, those were the ones who sold out. The market still looks good but it's not a runaway market."
The International Copper Study Group reported that world copper consumption in January and February was 7.5 percent higher than in the same two months in 1996.
July settled flat at 113.10 cents per pound, traded 114.00 to 112.10 cents. Spot May went out 0.60 cent weaker at 113.20 cents. Volume was estimated at 11,000 lots.
The LME cash to three months backwardation was $55/$59 by COMEX close, down from $61/$65 Monday.
COMEX copper stocks on Tuesday fell 1,407 short tons to 40,479 short tons. LME stocks on Tuesday rose 525 tonnes to 152,125 tonnes.
